title: NSCLC Checkpoint Inhibitor Overall-Survival Evidence Map (Provisional)
research_question: Do immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1/PD-L1) improve overall survival in adults with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC)?

scope.population: Adults with advanced/metastatic, resectable stage II, or unresectable stage III NSCLC evaluated for first-line, perioperative, or post-chemoradiotherapy consolidation immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, with population extensions explicitly separated when line of therapy, PD-L1 expression, liver metastases, or ECOG performance status changes applicability.
scope.intervention: PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab, durvalumab, cemiplimab, sintilimab, and pooled-class regimens), alone or combined with chemotherapy, VEGF-targeting antibodies, or dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade; agent-specific findings are kept separate from pooled-class findings.
scope.outcome: Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) versus chemotherapy alone or a non-ICI comparator; perioperative event-free survival, major pathological response, and pathological complete response for the resectable-disease branch. Safety/toxicity and comparisons between two active ICI regimens appear only as qualifying context, not as a primary claim.
scope.exclusions: No pediatric, driver-mutation-positive (EGFR/ALK-altered), or small-cell lung cancer population is represented. The PACIFIC trial itself -- the foundational RCT for durvalumab consolidation -- is not in this corpus (closed-access venue, no PMC OA record); real-world validations of it are represented instead. Cost-effectiveness and quality-of-life outcomes are not represented.

evidence_nodes.inclusion_rationale: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 randomized controlled trials (14,758 patients) finding PD-1 and PD-L1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy each improve overall survival versus chemotherapy alone in first-line advanced NSCLC -- the corpus's core pooled trial-level evidence.

Bayesian network meta-analysis of 20 RCTs restricted to driver-gene-negative NSCLC with liver metastases, extending the general ICI-plus-chemotherapy-versus-chemotherapy-alone PFS/OS finding to a specific, harder-to-treat subpopulation.

Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs (4,426 patients) isolating regimens that combine PD-1/PD-L1 blockade with VEGF/VEGFR-targeting antibodies -- a distinct intervention definition from single-class PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition, improving PFS and OS versus non-dual-targeting control.

Biomarker-stratified subgroup analysis of the ORIENT-11 trial (sintilimab plus chemotherapy) showing markedly larger PFS/OS benefit in ICPscore-high patients -- qualifies which patients within a single trial derive the largest benefit, not a new comparative claim.

Randomized, phase 3 KEYNOTE-671 clinical-stage-II subgroup (n=239) establishing the corpus's direct randomized evidence for perioperative pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in resectable disease, with event-free survival significantly improved though the OS subgroup estimate is not independently significant.

Prospective real-world CRISP registry (231 patients) extending durvalumab consolidation's PFS/OS benefit after chemoradiotherapy from PACIFIC's trial population (not itself in this corpus) to routine unresectable stage III practice.

Retrospective single-center cohort (142 patients) stratifying durvalumab-consolidation OS/PFS benefit by PD-L1 status, qualifying which post-chemoradiotherapy patients the consolidation finding applies to.

Small (n=34) real-world cohort using induction chemoimmunotherapy before consolidative radiotherapy -- an alternative treatment sequencing to the standard chemoradiotherapy-then-durvalumab-consolidation approach, contextualizing rather than replacing it.

Real-world cohort (610 evaluable of 684 patients across three Greek centers) finding immunotherapy at any treatment line associated with longer OS than chemotherapy alone, extending trial-level findings to unselected routine practice.

Swedish registry cohort (854 lung-cancer patients) reporting median overall survival on palliative ICI treatment stratified by baseline ECOG performance status, extending real-world context to performance-status subgroups without a concurrent non-ICI comparator.

Prognostic analysis within cemiplimab-treated patients (EMPOWER-Lung 1/3) showing composite patient-reported-outcome burden predicts OS -- a risk-stratification endpoint qualifier among ICI-treated patients, not a comparison against a non-ICI arm.

Retrospective single-center comparison (200 patients) of nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab-plus-chemotherapy against pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy finding no significant OS or time-to-discontinuation difference -- an active ICI-regimen-versus-ICI-regimen comparison, not evidence against ICI efficacy itself.

Pooled analysis of 12 real-world cohorts (17,506 PD-L1>=50% patients) on first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy reporting durable long-term outcomes (60-month OS rate 29.0%) -- single-arm, but the corpus's largest durability synthesis for high-PD-L1 monotherapy.

population_groups.label: First-line advanced/metastatic NSCLC, ICI(+chemotherapy) vs chemotherapy alone (randomized-trial-level evidence)
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: These are meta-analyses and one biomarker-stratified single-trial subgroup; agents, chemotherapy backbones, and captured subpopulations (liver metastases for Wu, PD-1/VEGF dual-targeting for Mao, ICPscore-high responders for Liao) differ and are not interchangeable.

population_groups.label: Advanced NSCLC, real-world/registry ICI cohorts (any line, unselected by trial eligibility)
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: Real-world cohorts reflect physician-selected populations, not randomized allocation; confounding by indication is a shared limitation. Machado and Gandara have no non-ICI comparator, and Weber compares two active ICI regimens rather than ICI versus chemotherapy alone.

population_groups.label: Resectable stage II or unresectable stage III NSCLC, perioperative/consolidation setting
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: This surgical/consolidation-setting population differs materially from the advanced/metastatic population above -- these records establish perioperative and post-chemoradiotherapy findings, not first-line metastatic-disease efficacy.

comparator_groups.label: Chemotherapy alone or no-ICI comparator (randomized or matched)
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The most direct comparative evidence for ICI benefit, but trial/cohort eligibility, dose, duration, and pooling heterogeneity remain material; several of these are real-world cohorts without randomization.

comparator_groups.label: No concurrent comparator (single-arm descriptive or within-cohort stratification)
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: These records describe outcomes within ICI-treated patients only (stratified by performance status, PRO burden, or treatment sequence) and cannot themselves demonstrate ICI superiority over an alternative.

comparator_groups.label: Active comparator (ICI regimen versus a different ICI regimen)
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Compares two active checkpoint-inhibitor-based regimens against each other, not against chemotherapy alone; a null result here does not contradict ICI-versus-chemotherapy evidence.

contradiction_assessment.statement: A bounded review of this corpus's 13 manually-reviewed NSCLC checkpoint-inhibitor records, completed 2026-08-10, found no result that directly contradicts the ICI(+chemotherapy)-versus-chemotherapy-alone or ICI-consolidation-versus-none overall-survival direction under a sufficiently aligned population, intervention, comparator, and outcome. Weber's null OS finding compares two active ICI regimens (nivolumab+ipilimumab+chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab+chemotherapy), not ICI versus a non-ICI comparator, and is an active-comparator qualifier, not a same-PICO contradiction. Stuschke's real-world OS difference did not reach statistical significance in its specific weighted analysis even though PFS did, which is a precision qualifier on a supporting result, not a direction reversal. Absence of an identified contradiction in this bounded, single-corpus search is not evidence that contradictory literature does not exist -- unlike the GLP-1 golden map, this search has not yet been independently re-run or extended to closed-access literature (e.g. the PACIFIC trial itself).

limitations: This map was compiled in a single AI-assisted authoring session from already-manually-reviewed (extraction_tier: manual) Evidence Records and their reviewed Relationship Records. A same-system record-to-source numerical fidelity check (2026-08-10) has since cross-checked every one of the 13 records' key claim_text/result_summary figures (hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, sample sizes) directly against the extracted source-PDF page text at each record's own source_span.page_number, and read all 9 relationship rationales for scientific coherence -- see review.notes for the two specific findings this surfaced. This is the same fidelity-check methodology GLP-1's map used, but it was performed by the same AI system (Claude) that compiled this map, not a genuinely independent reviewer (GLP-1's audit used a different AI system, OpenAI Codex); map_status therefore stays provisional until a genuinely independent second pass -- human or a different AI system -- repeats this check.

The direct randomized/meta-analytic evidence pools many distinct specific agents, chemotherapy backbones, and NSCLC subpopulations under each PD-1/PD-L1-class heading; agent-level and regimen-level differences are preserved in each record's own limitations but not separately re-verified here.
Five of thirteen records (Katsarolis, Nodbrant, Machado, Gandara, Esen) are real-world or single-arm observational cohorts vulnerable to confounding by indication and selection bias.

The PACIFIC trial itself, the foundational RCT establishing durvalumab consolidation after chemoradiotherapy, is not present in this corpus (closed-access venue); the perioperative/consolidation branch instead rests on real-world validations of it (Stuschke, Selke) and one alternative-sequencing cohort (Esen).

One of the thirteen manually-reviewed records (Weber's active-comparator study) is not yet connected to any other record by a reviewed relationship edge; it stands as independent context, not yet cross-referenced. Tsuboi's stage-II EFS/OS subgroup is now connected (`rel-onc-tsuboi-qualifies-dang-perioperative-os-001`, added 2026-08-10): it extends Dang's advanced-disease OS-benefit finding to a resectable, perioperative population, where OS is directionally favorable but not independently significant while EFS and pathologic response are clearly significant -- a qualifier, not a contradiction.
Access, cost, quality of life, and individual benefit-harm tradeoffs are not represented.
known_gaps: A record-to-source numerical fidelity check has now been performed for every selected record and relationship (2026-08-10, see review.notes), but by the same AI system that compiled this map -- a genuinely independent human or different-AI-system audit, matching the GLP-1 golden map's review process, has not yet been performed for this corpus.

The PACIFIC trial itself remains outside this corpus; acquiring it (or an equivalent open-access primary RCT for durvalumab consolidation) would let the perioperative/consolidation branch rest on randomized rather than only real-world evidence.
A reproducible, periodically-rerun same-PICO contradiction search (matching GLP-1's 2026-08-04 search) has not yet been established for this corpus.
Toxicity/adverse-event synthesis across the ICI regimens represented here is not yet built as its own qualifier layer.

Broader driver-mutation-positive (EGFR/ALK-altered) and small-cell lung cancer coverage remains out of scope for this corpus by design (see scope.exclusions) but is a real gap relative to the full clinical NSCLC/lung-cancer question.

Nodbrant's record cites confidence intervals, per-stratum patient counts, and 90-day mortality percentages from Table 2, but the 2026-08-10 fidelity check could only independently confirm the three headline median-OS figures (21.5/9.6/4.3 months) from the extracted page's prose -- the table itself did not extract as machine-readable text (a known limitation of this project's PDF text extraction for table regions), so those specific CI/n/mortality figures were not independently re-derived from the extracted text, only trusted from the record's own prior manual_source_audit.

review.method: Compiled from the corpus's existing manually-reviewed Evidence Records and their reviewed Relationship Records; this map-level synthesis (scope, population/comparator groupings, contradiction assessment) was authored once in a single AI-assisted session. A same-system record-to-source fidelity check (2026-08-10) subsequently read the extracted source-PDF page text at each of the 13 records' own source_span.page_number and cross-checked every claim_text/result_summary numerical figure (hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, sample sizes) against it, and read all 9 relationship rationales for scientific coherence against both endpoints' fields -- see notes below for what this found. The map's population/comparator groupings and contradiction assessment were not independently re-derived from scratch, only checked for internal consistency with the now-fidelity-checked records.
review.reviewed_by: Claude (session compilation, single-pass); record-fidelity check by Claude (same AI system, not an independent reviewer)
review.notes: Every evidence_record_id and relationship_id referenced here already exists as a manually-reviewed record or edge in the corpus (see evidence_records.jsonl/relationship_records.jsonl); this document adds map-level organization (scope, population/comparator groupings, contradiction assessment) on top of them, not new source claims. A same-day connectivity check found two of the thirteen nodes (Tsuboi, Weber) had zero relationship edges despite being included; Tsuboi's connectivity gap was closed with one new reviewed relationship (rel-onc-tsuboi-qualifies-dang-perioperative-os-001), authored by direct PICO/result_summary comparison against Dang, not automated candidate matching. Weber was deliberately left unconnected rather than force a relationship to a mismatched comparison axis. The 2026-08-10 fidelity check cross-referenced all 13 records' key figures against extracted source-page text and found all 13 faithfully represented, with two specific notes: (1) Liao's source PDF itself shows two slightly different renderings of the same low-ICPscore OS confidence interval in its running prose versus its figure legend (0.81-2.21 vs 0.81-2.12) -- a likely typo internal to the source PDF, not an evidence-record error, since the record's stated 0.81-2.12 matches the figure-legend rendering; (2) Nodbrant's record cites CI/n/mortality figures from a table that did not extract as machine-readable text, so only its three headline median-OS figures were independently re-confirmed from the extracted prose (see limitations/known_gaps for detail). This still does not meet the independent-reviewer bar the GLP-1 golden map's audit (a different AI system, OpenAI Codex) established -- map_status therefore stays provisional and review.status stays secondary_review_required until a genuinely independent (human or different-AI-system) pass repeats this check.
